text:
Reason that reigns in me,

why must I lie,

saying impassively no,

when the soul says yes?


On looking at your beautiful eyes

I feel joy being born,

because they turn, my life,

anger into enchantment.

On looking at your red lips

where love is treasured

my enslaved breast adores you,

and, fleeing frenzy,

I must exclaim, my lady,

“reason that reigns in me.”


If you observe in my countenance

the delirium you inspire,

if you look at me with delight

and in my throbbing breast

perceive the sweet instant

you cause in my soul,

what is it worth that I feign calm!

if the fire that consumed me

triumphantly wins the palm,

why should I lie?


Oh! do not expect

the ardent breast to deny it;

so sweet an affection

cannot be hidden; to silence it

is to suffer and increase it:

for in vain, O God, would I lie

if, when asked someday

whether my heart adored you,

I answered, my soul,

saying impassively, NO.


It would be as good as denying

that you are beautiful and alluring,

that dawn appears evasive

if it sees your eyes shine;

it would be as good as claiming

that one who came to behold you

managed to live and forget you,

could manage to live without you,

if I said NO to loving you

when the soul says YES.

translation.title: Gloss
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the repeated yes/no refrain and the source’s glosa-like stanza progression; rhyme is allowed to yield to clarity in English.
